intro: High on its cliff, a fortress looks down on you. This is Tlos Ancient City, in Muğla province, one of the oldest and largest cities of Lycia. Its story runs from the 2nd millennium BC through the Lycian and Roman periods, and its emblem is a rock tomb carved with Bellerophon. Let us climb into its past.
history: Tlos was one of the six founding cities of the Lycian League, and people have lived here without a break for more than 4,000 years. Under Roman rule it grew into a major metropolis of the region and a leading member of the League. Even then its story was not over: the fortress on the acropolis stayed in use through the Byzantine and Ottoman periods.
structure-1: You are now before the Bellerophon Rock Tomb, the icon of Tlos. Look closely at its façade: the relief shows Bellerophon with Pegasus, the hero and his horse carved into the living rock.
structure-2: Now raise your eyes to the Acropolis Fortress. Set on a high rock, it was built for defence, and from its height it once watched over the whole city.
structure-5: Here stands the Temple of Kronos, dedicated to the Titan god Kronos. Pause for a moment and imagine the offerings once brought to this ancient deity.
highlights: As you wander through Tlos, don't miss the Theatre, and then make your way on to the Stadium.
facts: Did you know? In mythology Tlos is regarded as the city of the hero Bellerophon, who killed the Chimera with his winged horse Pegasus. Fittingly, one of the rock tombs on the acropolis carries a relief of Bellerophon mounted on Pegasus. Tlos is one of Lycia's oldest cities, inhabited without a break for four thousand years, and a nineteenth-century Ottoman lord's castle crowns its acropolis.
outro: This brings our tour of Tlos Ancient City to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have stood for centuries; let them stand for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
